think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 39-year-old rural dog owner presents with indolent abdominal distention and multifocal intra-abdominal calcified cystic masses involving both the hepatic parenchyma and the pelvic mesentery/perivesical space. Multifocal peritoneal and visceral masses typically raise grave concern for metastatic peritoneal carcinomatosis, mesenchymal sarcoma, or congenital mesenteric cysts; however, entirely normal inflammatory/liver enzymes and rural canine exposure point to simultaneous visceral and peritoneal parasitic disease.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission evaluation concludes after documenting the 1-year chronology, rural canine exposure, normal baseline labs (absence of eosinophilia, normal transaminases and CRP), and CT imaging identifying the hepatic and mesenteric/pelvic masses, prior to send-out Echinococcus ELISA serology and exploratory laparotomy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Peritoneal carcinomatosis or cystic neoplasms (e.g., gastrointestinal stromal tumor or mesenteric lymphangioma) present with multifocal intra-abdominal masses but lack distinctive internal lamellated daughter cysts and calcified walls; positive parasite serology and pathognomonic cystic architecture rule out malignant processes.
case_prompt: A 39-year-old male presented with a 1-year history of mild, gradually worsening abdominal distention and pain localized predominantly to the right upper abdomen. The symptoms were unrelated to food intake, and he reported no history of fever, weight loss, previous surgeries, or significant medical conditions. Epidemiologically, he resided in a rural area and owned two dogs. Physical examination was unremarkable except for mild upper abdominal distension and discomfort. Initial laboratory blood tests were within normal reference ranges: white blood cell count 10,900/mcL (57.7% neutrophils, 0.7% eosinophils), AST 20 U/L, ALT 22 U/L, GGT 19 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 111 U/L, and a negative quantitative C-reactive protein. Upper abdominal ultrasound revealed a vague hepatic lesion. An abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan showed a large hepatic mass (9.5 cm x 6.2 cm x 6.8 cm) with a hyperdense wall and multiple internal calcifications, a similar well-circumscribed mass associated with an ileal loop exerting extrinsic mass effect on the urinary bladder (5.3 cm x 3.6 cm x 9.0 cm), and a third smaller, completely calcified lesion (2.3 cm x 2.0 cm x 2.5 cm) adjacent to the right side of the urinary bladder.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because of multifocal masses involving both the liver and the pelvic ileal mesentery; ruled out by entirely normal inflammatory markers, lack of constitutional symptoms or primary mucosal tumor, and absence of malignant cells on histopathology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Laboratory blood examination showed results within normal ranges (white blood cells 10.90 K/microL with 57.7% neutrophils, SGOT 20 U/L, SGPT 22 U/L, gamma-GT 19 U/L, ALP 111 U/L, and negative quantitative C.R.P. test).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the well-circumscribed, cystic lesion compressing the urinary bladder in a young adult; ruled out by concurrent presence of a large calcified hepatic lesion with daughter cysts and positive zoonotic serology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Level of eosinophils cells was normal (0.7%), while eosinophilia is present only in 25-40% of all patients.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic turning point was combining the patient's rural canine contact with CT findings of a calcified multi-vesicular hepatic cyst and mesenteric lesions, confirmed by positive anti-Echinococcus ELISA IgG serology and intraoperative extraction of characteristic lamellated ectocysts and daughter cysts.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: blood control for echinococcal antibodies (considering the patient's history of having dogs in his surroundings and the rather endemic presence of the disease in his area) was positive.

editor_comments: Distilled strictly to baseline admission presentation and imaging. Simultaneous hepatic and pelvic-mesenteric hydatid cysts mimicking multifocal peritoneal carcinomatosis; confirmed by serology and laparotomy.
